text:
ConocoPhillips edged up 0.28% today, a small gain that marks a modest recovery after the stock fell 3.9% over the two prior days (November 23–24). The bounce came as oil prices stabilized: US crude held at $82.24 per barrel while global oil prices rose to $92.94, suggesting some steadying in the market after recent volatility. This modest recovery fits the pattern of the broader energy sector stabilizing after a dip.

The backdrop remains challenging for the stock. The collapse of draft climate language at COP31 that failed to address fossil fuels—a major story on the same day as today's gain—reflects ongoing uncertainty around long-term energy policy that weighs on oil and gas valuations. While near-term oil price stability may have supported today's small rebound, the two-week decline of 2.06% reflects investor concern about the regulatory and climate headwinds facing the sector.
